newsitem.title: UK: London gold slips to lowest fix since November 93.
newsitem.headline: London gold slips to lowest fix since November 93.

text.p: Gold was fixed at its lowest level since November 3, 1993 on Thursday afternoon, after light fund selling took the market lower in New York, dealers said.
Bullion fixed at $366.55 per ounce after $367.80 in the morning and $369.55 at its pre-holiday fixing on Tuesday.
On November 3, 1993, gold was fixed at $363.00.
"We saw some fund selling on Comex just before the fixing. Before that there really wasn't any direction in the market after the holidays," one dealer said.
Gold had been very quiet during European trading as dealers waited to see what direction came from Comex.
The February Comex futures contract ended down $2.00 at $369.20 on Tuesday, with most of the selling coming in the closing minutes of the session.
Shortly after the fixing, February gold futures were off $1.00 at $368.20.
Some dealers questioned whether the move on Tuesday and this afternoon represented a serious retrenchment for the gold price.
"It may be a bear trap," one dealer said.
Another issue which caused caution about gold's weak start to the new year was platinum extending its premium over gold, having been flat to discounted in the final weeks of 1996.
"You can't see gold turning round while platinum is at a discount. Now that platinum is back above it, that is another reason for doubting how far gold will fall," a dealer said.
Dealers said spot gold had found support at $366.00, the day's low bid.
Even so, the outlook for gold was still largely bearish. "A gold clear-out would be good for gold. I can see it down to $330-$340 in the early part of this year," one dealer said.
Dealers said the firmer palladium price was helping to support its sister metal, platinum.
Palladium bucked the generally weaker trend by fixing at its highest level since September 19, 1996 at $120.75, up from $116.50 before the New York break.
Dealers said palladium saw buying on Nymex on Tuesday when the March futures contract closed up $5.25 at $124.25.
Concerns about the continuing availability of Russian exports and substitution of palladium in many applications for mre expensive sister metal platinum were behind the move.
Platinum was indicated at $369.00/$370.00, down about $1.00 cents from Tuesday's level, while silver attracted little interest at $4.77/$4.79, off a couple of cents.
